body_ar:
لقد اهتم العلماء بالعلم حتى ألفوا فيه منظومات يسهل حفظها وفهم مضمونها، والشيخ هنا يشرح بعض أبيات من منظومة في العقائد، بين فيها معرفة الله من جهة وجوبها وطريقة تحصيلها.
الغاية والهدف من دراسة علم العقائد:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فقد من الله علينا بإكمال شرح نظم الشيخ المتعلق بالعقائد، وقد ترك الشيخ حفظه الله تعالى التفصيل في بعض المسائل اعتماداً على تفصيل ذكره في نظمه لجامع خليل ، فإن أصل الكتاب كان نظماً لمختصر خليل في الفقه المالكي، وكذلك نظم في آخره الجامع لـخليل نفسه. هذا الجامع كتاب يجمع العقائد والآداب والأخلاق الشرعية، وكثيراً من الأحكام المتعلقة بالسلوك عموماً، قد نظمه الشيخ في حوالي خمسمائة بيت، والمبحث العقدي منه بين أيدينا اليوم، وهو أبيات قليلة تضيف بعض التفصيلات لما سبق...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The scholars gave such care to knowledge that they composed versifications of it, easy to memorise and whose content is easy to understand. Here the Sheikh explains some lines from a versification on the articles of creed, in which he sets out the knowledge of God in respect of its being obligatory and of the way it is attained.

## The end and purpose of studying the science of creed

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God has favoured us with the completion of the commentary on the Sheikh's versification of the articles of creed. The Sheikh, may God preserve him, left some questions without detailed treatment, relying on the detail he gave in his versification of Khalil's Jāmiʿ — for the original of the book was a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil on Maliki jurisprudence, and at its end he likewise versified the Jāmiʿ of Khalil himself. This Jāmiʿ is a book that brings together the articles of creed, the proprieties, the moral qualities the law enjoins, and a great many of the rulings that bear on conduct generally. The Sheikh put it into verse in about five hundred lines; and the section of it dealing with creed is what is before us today — a small number of lines which add some particulars to what has gone before …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the end of the introductory remarks, before a single line of the creed section is quoted, so that neither the obligation of knowing God nor the way it is attained — the two subjects the synopsis announces — is reached. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-37.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: فقد من الله علينا بإكمال شرح نظم الشيخ ... وقد ترك الشيخ حفظه الله تعالى التفصيل
flags.context: the opening of the transcribed portion
options: read 'the Sheikh' as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read 'the Sheikh' as the lecturer himself
flags.note: This record is what settles the referent of 'الشيخ' for the whole of the creed run, IDs 707-721, and it is worth a reviewer's attention for that reason alone. The speaker here says that God has favoured 'us' with completing the commentary on 'the Sheikh's versification', and then describes what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed. A commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text in the third person while commenting on it, and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' is the living author of the versified base text, and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named and the Sheikh's office should confirm the identification before publication.

flags.context: the site's synopsis, describing what the base text sets out
options: the knowledge of God in respect of its being obligatory
knowledge of God as regards the obligation of it
knowledge of God with respect to its necessity
flags.note: A ruling word in a creedal setting, where style guide section 8 has to be checked before the five-rulings table is applied — but the subject here is an act of a responsible person, knowing God, and not a proposition about God, so the legal reading stands and 'obligatory' is right. The third option is recorded because the obligation of knowing God is the classical dispute between those who ground it in reason and those who ground it in revelation, and 'necessity' would prejudge that dispute toward the rational side. The served text never reaches the question.

flags.context: the description of the contents of Khalil's Jāmiʿ
options: the proprieties, the moral qualities the law enjoins
manners and the ethics of the law
flags.note: 'آداب' is rendered 'proprieties' — the disciplines proper to an activity — consistently with record 700 of the preceding slice, where the same choice was made and 'etiquette' rejected as too slight. 'الشرعية' qualifies both nouns and is rendered as a relative clause, since the English adjective 'legal' would suggest positive law.

flags.arabic: وكثيراً من الأحكام المتعلقة بالسلوك عموماً
flags.context: the description of the contents of Khalil's Jāmiʿ
options: a great many of the rulings that bear on conduct generally
many rulings relating to spiritual wayfaring in general
flags.note: 'سلوك' is ambiguous between conduct in the ordinary sense and the technical sense of wayfaring on the spiritual path, which is the sense it carries in record 715 of this same run ('أهل السلوك'). Here it is listed after creed, proprieties and moral qualities, in a description of a Maliki compendium, which favours the ordinary sense; but the second reading is live and is recorded rather than suppressed.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.

The bibliographically most useful record in the run: it names the base text and its structure — a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq on Maliki jurisprudence, with the same author's versification of Khalil's Jāmiʿ appended at the end in some five hundred lines, whose creed section is what these lessons expound.
Proper names are given without diacritics in body text per style guide section 2: Khalil ibn Ishaq, al-Maqqari, al-Ashʿari. 'الجامع' is kept as 'Jāmiʿ' because it is a book title.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record. The one ruling word, 'وجوبها', is the site's and is treated in its own flag.
